title: Market Metro — Agentic Commerce That Learns

style.captions: Two lines maximum; keep disclosures readable
style.motion: Slow push-ins, brief highlights and clean cuts; do not fabricate UI actions

production.stage: Merchant-led product showcase preview complete; final MP4 not exported

production.story: Form & Function and a shopper who went quiet; narrative visuals are illustrative, supporting clips are recorded app evidence.

scenes.title: Meet Form & Function
scenes.captureAction: Wide market opening dissolves into a clean close-up of the actual shop renderer. Large merchant-focused typography; no website chrome.
scenes.narration: The doors are open. The shelves are ready. But some shoppers have gone quiet. Meet Form and Function, a furniture shop inside our simulated Market Metro.

scenes.title: A shopper goes quiet
scenes.captureAction: Show Shopper 179 and an animated 16-day market purchase gap. Do not imply permanent churn or a store-specific purchase history.
scenes.narration: Shopper one seventy nine has not bought in sixteen days. Which product would bring them back? And how can a merchant know the next campaign will be worth it?

scenes.title: Keep the meaning intact
scenes.captureAction: Animate one checkout splitting into two merchant portions, then cut into the recorded ambiguity hold.
scenes.narration: A single checkout can split into several merchant orders. Our ontology keeps the meaning intact: one purchase, counted once. If the links are unclear, the system holds the decision.

scenes.title: Turn activity into a plan
scenes.captureAction: Animate observed demand, inventory and past responses feeding one planner and local training tools. Show a short close-up of the real recorded decision.
scenes.narration: Market Metro turns those questions into a plan. The language model investigates demand, chooses twenty eight days of history, and requests two model fits. It proposes recommendations and shopping needs inquiries for consenting shoppers. Every choice is recorded, and every campaign must pass a financial test.
onScreen: AG Studio · model registry and recorded decisions

scenes.title: Test before launch
scenes.captureAction: Reveal the two development-trial outcomes and the selected ranking, using the saved numerical evidence.
scenes.narration: The planner preferred one model. The verifier tested both rankings on separate trial markets. Boosted trees earned more while protecting merchant outcomes, so it became the selected model. Measure first. Then launch.
onScreen: Selected before measuring this market’s later outcomes

scenes.title: The shopper returns
scenes.captureAction: Show the shop and returning avatar, a clearly illustrated side table, the $96 purchase and day-36 delivery. Retain a recorded app cut-in.
scenes.narration: On day thirty five, the recommendation meets a need in the simulation. Our quiet shopper chooses a mobile side table from Form and Function, pays ninety six dollars, and receives it the next day. Under fixed rules, that request went unfilled.

scenes.title: Payment verified
scenes.captureAction: Make PayPal and the $96 test capture the hero. Reveal the fee and merchant proceeds, then show the real receipt and warehouse linkage.
scenes.narration: That exact order was mirrored once through PayPal Sandbox. A completed ninety six dollar capture. Three fifty six in fees, and ninety two forty four for the test merchant. One order, one receipt, linked back to the warehouse.
onScreen: One existing sale; never counted twice

scenes.title: A measured result
scenes.captureAction: Reveal +16 retained purchases, +$114.96 modeled PayPal net and +$1,024.86 merchant contribution across the full 12-store market.
scenes.narration: Across the twelve store market, this campaign delivered sixteen extra retained purchases. Merchant contribution grew by over a thousand dollars. Modeled PayPal net rose three point four seven percent after model cost. These are simulated results, not production profit.
onScreen: One paired simulation · contribution includes inventory

scenes.title: Open the evidence
scenes.captureAction: Use enlarged native AG Grid sorting, a decision drill-down, the PayPal custom widget and a real dashboard resize.
scenes.narration: AG Grid and AG Charts make every step inspectable. Compare models. Open the agent's evidence. Check the native PayPal receipt in our custom widget. Even the dashboard layout is editable. The story ends with a sale, and a record you can verify.
onScreen: AG Studio · AG Grid · AG Charts
Inspect models → explain decisions → reconcile payments
Custom PayPal widget · editable dashboard layout

uploadDraft.title: Market Metro | Agentic Commerce That Learns | PayPal AI Hackathon
uploadDraft.description:
Market Metro turns observed merchant activity into trained models, tested campaigns and traceable PayPal payments. This demo follows one saved 12-store, 600-shopper simulation from Day 1 to a recorded agent decision, purchase and native PayPal Sandbox receipt.

Against fixed rules in that same simulation: 16 more retained purchases, $1,024.86 additional merchant contribution, and $114.96 higher modeled PayPal net after estimated model cost. Merchant contribution includes inventory value. These are simulated outcomes, not actual PayPal profit. The $96 Sandbox capture is an existing order and uses fictitious funds.

Built with PayPal Sandbox, Gemini on Vertex AI, local scikit-learn models, SQLite, Three.js and AG Studio with native AG Grid, AG Charts and a custom PayPal evidence widget. The ontology feed comparison is a separate synthetic-data test.

Source and setup: https://github.com/VinceVence/market-metro
Original code: MIT. Third-party components retain their own licenses.
